title: State init must match DOM init
trigger: Two sources of truth (a state variable and a DOM property) must be synchronized at init — otherwise the first toggle goes the wrong direction.
principle: When a state variable and a DOM property both track visibility, they must start in sync. If DOM is display:none, state must be false; if DOM is display:flex, state must be true. Otherwise the first toggle flips state but DOM doesn't change (or vice versa). Prefer a single source of truth.

cases.context: Overlay state initialized true but DOM display:none — first 'w' keypress sets state false (display stays none, no change), second press sets true (display block) — needs 2 presses
Panel state false and DOM display:none after import — panel never auto-shows because state stays false
Old persisted settings lack a new field — consumer calls .find() on undefined and crashes
cases.bad:
// Every consumer guards individually — N guards, easy to miss one
const shortcut = settings.keyboardShortcuts?.find(s => s.key === 'w') ?? defaultShortcut;

applyFor: Content script state (closure variables + DOM style) — Chrome extension, userscript
React state vs DOM ref (useState + useRef + imperative DOM mutation)
Storage migration (old settings missing new field → fill defaults at migration, not guard each consumer)
Any UI with 2 sources of truth: state variable + DOM property must sync at init
